purpose: Teach: 群衆/語源/裏切っ/献血/くくっ/苑/龍/埋もれ

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、革命時の群衆心理を論文で扱っていましたね
lines.en: Ren, you were working on a paper about crowd psychology during the revolution, weren't you?
lines.style: Warm, steady teacher voice. Genuine curiosity without pressure. Slight rise at the end — inviting him to confirm. She's already read his work.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、漢字の語源を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, actually my paper was on the etymology of kanji.
lines.style: Quiet correction, not defensive. He's used to being misunderstood and accepts it without complaint. Slight hesitation — choosing his words carefully. Eyes brief contact.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 同盟国に裏切った国家を論文で扱っていましたね
lines.en: And you covered the nation that betrayed its allies, didn't you?
lines.style: Patient, thoughtful pause before speaking. She's testing whether he'll correct her again. Warm but observant — noticing his pattern. Not unkind.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、災害時の献血運動を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Actually, my paper focused on blood donation campaigns during disaster relief.
lines.style: Mild, persistent correction. Still earnest, not frustrated. He doesn't perform exasperation. Just states what is true. Slight weariness under the gentleness.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、紐をくくった結び目の文化史を論文で扱っていましたね
lines.en: Ren, I recall you exploring the cultural history of knots and knot-tying, yes?
lines.style: She's leaning in slightly now, still warm but with an undercurrent of intention. Testing him one more time. A teacher's careful observation of a student's patience.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、宮内苑の歴史を論文で扱いました
lines.en: No, my paper was actually on the history of the imperial gardens.
lines.style: Still polite, still earnest, but a hairline shift — he's been corrected (or correcting) three times now and it shows in his breath. Not angry. Just the quiet tiredness of being heard differently.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 龍の伝承を論文で扱っていましたね
lines.en: You explored dragon folklore in your research, didn't you?
lines.style: She shifts here — warmer, more engaged, almost conspiratorial. Not testing anymore. Recognition dawning. Her tone lifts slightly, inviting him in rather than checking him.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、書庫に埋もれた古文書を論文で扱いました
lines.en: My paper was on ancient documents buried in the archives.
lines.style: Quieter now, almost to himself. The final correction carries a gentle exhaustion. He's patient but there's a hairline fracture of hope — maybe this time she'll hear him. Trailing soft.
